1	# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
12	- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
13	- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
14	- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
15	- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation
16	
17	## Requirements & Constraints
18	
19	- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
20	- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
21	- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
22	- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
23	- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
24	- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
25	- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
26	- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
27	- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
28	- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
29	- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.
30	
31	## Technical Decisions
32	
33	- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
34	- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
35	- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
36	- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
37	- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
38	- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
39	- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
40	- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
41	- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
46	- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
47	- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
48	- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
49	- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
50	- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
51	- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
56	- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
57	- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
58	- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.
59

- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.

## Intent

**Problem:** A user's own reflective Chat Message can't become a journal Entry without retyping it — `ChatUiMessage` has no bookmark affordance, `EntriesRepository.create()` has no `chatMessageId` slot even though `Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already reserve it, and `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` is still an `UnimplementedError` stub explicitly waiting for this story.

**Approach:** Add a four-state (`idle`/`saving`/`saved`/`error`) bookmark button to user-only chat bubbles. `ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage(messageId)` calls the real `isolatedSideEffect` (replacing the stub) wrapping a call to a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — the shared interface AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires — which itself wraps `EntriesRepository.create(..., source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: ...)`. `ChatCubit` never imports `EntriesRepository` or anything under `entries/data`/`entries/presentation`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Bookmark affordance: `ChatMessageRole.user` bubbles only.
- `ChatCubit` depends on `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — never `EntriesRepository` directly, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (AGENTS.md: "RF10 must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly").
- Save runs through `isolatedSideEffect` (real body, replacing the `UnimplementedError` stub), awaited before bookmark state updates.
- Tapping `saved` is a client-side no-op; repeat backend calls for the same `chatMessageId` are themselves idempotent (200, not 409 — `openapi.yaml`'s `entries.create` doc) so no extra client dedup needed.
- A save failure never freezes the session: only the tapped bubble's state flips to `error` (retryable); composer/history/other bubbles unaffected.
- Icon + color together, never color alone: `idle` outline, `saving` spinner (static label under Reduce Motion), `saved` ochre check (`colorAccent`, `0xFFC98A3E`), `error` red warning (`colorError`). Tap target ≥44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
- Bookmarking requires a non-null `serverId` (the id sent as `chatMessageId`); tapping before that is a no-op, mirroring `retryMessage`'s guard.
- Both of `bookmarkMessage`'s `emit()` calls (before and after the `isolatedSideEffect` await) check `isClosed` first — not just the one after the await.
- A bookmark glyph's Reduce-Motion static label sits in a width-capped slot (e.g. wrapped the same way `bubbleContainer` is `Flexible`-constrained), so it cannot squeeze the message bubble under large accessibility text scaling.

**Ask First:** none — `chatMessageId` on `create()` is a pre-reserved slot (`Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already exist for this story), not a new architectural call.

**Never:**
- Never import `EntriesRepository`, `entries/data/`, or `entries/presentation/` from `chat/` — only `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`.
- Never route the bookmark save through `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — its `create()` clears *any* app-wide failed pending-write on each call (written for exactly one capture flow in flight at a time), so a concurrent chat bookmark could silently clear an unrelated capture flow's visible error card.
- Never persist bookmark state across restarts — in-memory only; a stale `idle` post-reload is harmless given backend idempotency.
- Never let a bookmark failure disable the composer or affect other bubbles.
- Never introduce a second Entry model or bypass `EntriesRepository` (the use case's own only caller).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path | Tap bookmark on a user bubble with `serverId` set, `idle` | Bubble flips `idle` → `saving` → `saved` (ochre check); `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase(content, chatMessageId: serverId)` called once | N/A |
| Already saved | Tap a `saved` bubble | No-op — no new call, no state change | N/A |
| No serverId yet | Tap bookmark before `message_created` SSE event set `serverId` | No-op — same guard shape as `retryMessage` | N/A |
| Save fails | `create()` resolves `Left(Failure)` | Bubble flips to `error` (red warning); rest of session (composer, other bubbles, scroll) unaffected | Tapping `error` re-attempts the same save, returning to `saving` |
| Side-effect throws | `action()` inside `isolatedSideEffect` throws synchronously or async | Caught, mapped to `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, never propagates to caller | Bubble flips to `error`, same as above |
| Second tap while saving | Tap bookmark again while a save is already in flight for that message | No-op (re-entrancy guard, mirrors `_isSending`-style check scoped to that message) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). 51	+## Intent
52	+
53	+**Problem:** A user's own reflective Chat Message can't become a journal Entry without retyping it — `ChatUiMessage` has no bookmark affordance, `EntriesRepository.create()` has no `chatMessageId` slot even though `Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already reserve it, and `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` is still an `UnimplementedError` stub explicitly waiting for this story.
54	+
55	+**Approach:** Add a four-state (`idle`/`saving`/`saved`/`error`) bookmark button to user-only chat bubbles. `ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage(messageId)` calls the real `isolatedSideEffect` (replacing the stub) wrapping a call to a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — the shared interface AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires — which itself wraps `EntriesRepository.create(..., source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: ...)`. `ChatCubit` never imports `EntriesRepository` or anything under `entries/data`/`entries/presentation`.
56	+
57	+## Boundaries & Constraints
58	+
59	+**Always:**
60	+- Bookmark affordance: `ChatMessageRole.user` bubbles only.
61	+- `ChatCubit` depends on `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — never `EntriesRepository` directly, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (AGENTS.md: "RF10 must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly").
62	+- Save runs through `isolatedSideEffect` (real body, replacing the `UnimplementedError` stub), awaited before bookmark state updates.
63	+- Tapping `saved` is a client-side no-op; repeat backend calls for the same `chatMessageId` are themselves idempotent (200, not 409 — `openapi.yaml`'s `entries.create` doc) so no extra client dedup needed.
64	+- A save failure never freezes the session: only the tapped bubble's state flips to `error` (retryable); composer/history/other bubbles unaffected.
65	+- Icon + color together, never color alone: `idle` outline, `saving` spinner (static label under Reduce Motion), `saved` ochre check (`colorAccent`, `0xFFC98A3E`), `error` red warning (`colorError`). Tap target ≥44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
66	+- Bookmarking requires a non-null `serverId` (the id sent as `chatMessageId`); tapping before that is a no-op, mirroring `retryMessage`'s guard.
67	+- Both of `bookmarkMessage`'s `emit()` calls (before and after the `isolatedSideEffect` await) check `isClosed` first — not just the one after the await.
68	+- A bookmark glyph's Reduce-Motion static label sits in a width-capped slot (e.g. wrapped the same way `bubbleContainer` is `Flexible`-constrained), so it cannot squeeze the message bubble under large accessibility text scaling.
69	+
70	+**Ask First:** none — `chatMessageId` on `create()` is a pre-reserved slot (`Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already exist for this story), not a new architectural call.
71	+
72	+**Never:**
73	+- Never import `EntriesRepository`, `entries/data/`, or `entries/presentation/` from `chat/` — only `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`.
74	+- Never route the bookmark save through `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — its `create()` clears *any* app-wide failed pending-write on each call (written for exactly one capture flow in flight at a time), so a concurrent chat bookmark could silently clear an unrelated capture flow's visible error card.
75	+- Never persist bookmark state across restarts — in-memory only; a stale `idle` post-reload is harmless given backend idempotency.
76	+- Never let a bookmark failure disable the composer or affect other bubbles.
77	+- Never introduce a second Entry model or bypass `EntriesRepository` (the use case's own only caller).

79	+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
80	+
81	+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
82	+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
83	+| Happy path | Tap bookmark on a user bubble with `serverId` set, `idle` | Bubble flips `idle` → `saving` → `saved` (ochre check); `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase(content, chatMessageId: serverId)` called once | N/A |
84	+| Already saved | Tap a `saved` bubble | No-op — no new call, no state change | N/A |
85	+| No serverId yet | Tap bookmark before `message_created` SSE event set `serverId` | No-op — same guard shape as `retryMessage` | N/A |
86	+| Save fails | `create()` resolves `Left(Failure)` | Bubble flips to `error` (red warning); rest of session (composer, other bubbles, scroll) unaffected | Tapping `error` re-attempts the same save, returning to `saving` |
87	+| Side-effect throws | `action()` inside `isolatedSideEffect` throws synchronously or async | Caught, mapped to `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, never propagates to caller | Bubble flips to `error`, same as above |
88	+| Second tap while saving | Tap bookmark again while a save is already in flight for that message | No-op (re-entrancy guard, mirrors `_isSending`-style check scoped to that message) | N/A |

+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** A user's own reflective Chat Message can't become a journal Entry without retyping it — `ChatUiMessage` has no bookmark affordance, `EntriesRepository.create()` has no `chatMessageId` slot even though `Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already reserve it, and `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` is still an `UnimplementedError` stub explicitly waiting for this story.
+
+**Approach:** Add a four-state (`idle`/`saving`/`saved`/`error`) bookmark button to user-only chat bubbles. `ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage(messageId)` calls the real `isolatedSideEffect` (replacing the stub) wrapping a call to a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — the shared interface AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires — which itself wraps `EntriesRepository.create(..., source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: ...)`. `ChatCubit` never imports `EntriesRepository` or anything under `entries/data`/`entries/presentation`.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Bookmark affordance: `ChatMessageRole.user` bubbles only.
+- `ChatCubit` depends on `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — never `EntriesRepository` directly, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (AGENTS.md: "RF10 must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly").
+- Save runs through `isolatedSideEffect` (real body, replacing the `UnimplementedError` stub), awaited before bookmark state updates.
+- Tapping `saved` is a client-side no-op; repeat backend calls for the same `chatMessageId` are themselves idempotent (200, not 409 — `openapi.yaml`'s `entries.create` doc) so no extra client dedup needed.
+- A save failure never freezes the session: only the tapped bubble's state flips to `error` (retryable); composer/history/other bubbles unaffected.
+- Icon + color together, never color alone: `idle` outline, `saving` spinner (static label under Reduce Motion), `saved` ochre check (`colorAccent`, `0xFFC98A3E`), `error` red warning (`colorError`). Tap target ≥44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
+- Bookmarking requires a non-null `serverId` (the id sent as `chatMessageId`); tapping before that is a no-op, mirroring `retryMessage`'s guard.
+- Both of `bookmarkMessage`'s `emit()` calls (before and after the `isolatedSideEffect` await) check `isClosed` first — not just the one after the await.
+- A bookmark glyph's Reduce-Motion static label sits in a width-capped slot (e.g. wrapped the same way `bubbleContainer` is `Flexible`-constrained), so it cannot squeeze the message bubble under large accessibility text scaling.
+
+**Ask First:** none — `chatMessageId` on `create()` is a pre-reserved slot (`Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already exist for this story), not a new architectural call.
+
+**Never:**
+- Never import `EntriesRepository`, `entries/data/`, or `entries/presentation/` from `chat/` — only `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`.
+- Never route the bookmark save through `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — its `create()` clears *any* app-wide failed pending-write on each call (written for exactly one capture flow in flight at a time), so a concurrent chat bookmark could silently clear an unrelated capture flow's visible error card.
+- Never persist bookmark state across restarts — in-memory only; a stale `idle` post-reload is harmless given backend idempotency.
+- Never let a bookmark failure disable the composer or affect other bubbles.
+- Never introduce a second Entry model or bypass `EntriesRepository` (the use case's own only caller).

+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| Happy path | Tap bookmark on a user bubble with `serverId` set, `idle` | Bubble flips `idle` → `saving` → `saved` (ochre check); `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase(content, chatMessageId: serverId)` called once | N/A |
+| Already saved | Tap a `saved` bubble | No-op — no new call, no state change | N/A |
+| No serverId yet | Tap bookmark before `message_created` SSE event set `serverId` | No-op — same guard shape as `retryMessage` | N/A |
+| Save fails | `create()` resolves `Left(Failure)` | Bubble flips to `error` (red warning); rest of session (composer, other bubbles, scroll) unaffected | Tapping `error` re-attempts the same save, returning to `saving` |
+| Side-effect throws | `action()` inside `isolatedSideEffect` throws synchronously or async | Caught, mapped to `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, never propagates to caller | Bubble flips to `error`, same as above |
+| Second tap while saving | Tap bookmark again while a save is already in flight for that message | No-op (re-entrancy guard, mirrors `_isSending`-style check scoped to that message) | N/A |

+/// `const factory` constructors on the base class so call sites read as
+/// `BookmarkState.idle()` rather than naming each subclass directly.
+/// Never persisted across restarts (Never) — in-memory only, on
+/// `ChatUiMessage.bookmarkState`.
+sealed class BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkState();
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.idle() = BookmarkIdle;
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.saving() = BookmarkSaving;
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.saved() = BookmarkSaved;
+
+  const factory BookmarkState.error(Failure failure) = BookmarkError;
+}
+
+/// The default state — outline icon, tappable.
+class BookmarkIdle extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkIdle();
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) => other is BookmarkIdle;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => (BookmarkIdle).hashCode;
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'BookmarkIdle()';
+}
+
+/// The save is in flight — spinner (or a static label under Reduce
+/// Motion, `ChatBubble`'s own concern, not this state's).
+class BookmarkSaving extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkSaving();
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) => other is BookmarkSaving;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => (BookmarkSaving).hashCode;
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'BookmarkSaving()';
+}
+
+/// The save succeeded — ochre check (`colorAccent`). Tapping an already-
+/// [BookmarkSaved] bubble is a client-side no-op (Boundaries).
+class BookmarkSaved extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkSaved();
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) => other is BookmarkSaved;
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => (BookmarkSaved).hashCode;
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'BookmarkSaved()';
+}
+
+/// The save failed — red warning, retryable: tapping it re-attempts the
+/// same save (I/O matrix: "Save fails"). [failure] is kept for parity with
+/// `SyncBadgeError`'s own shape, even though `ChatBubble` only ever needs
+/// the state's own identity (icon/color), never [failure]'s own message —
+/// no UI surface for it exists in this story's Boundaries.
+class BookmarkError extends BookmarkState {
+  const BookmarkError(this.failure);
+
+  final Failure failure;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      identical(this, other) ||
+      (other is BookmarkError && other.failure == failure);
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => failure.hashCode;
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'BookmarkError(failure: $failure)';
+}

The guard immediately before the first `emit(... saving ...)` (i.e., `bookmarkMessage` called when the cubit is already closed) has no dedicated test.

Under combined Reduce Motion + large accessibility text scaling, `TextOverflow.ellipsis` will truncate the word well before 64pt is reached, potentially rendering an unreadable fragment — which undercuts the very purpose of giving Reduce-Motion users a readable static indicator instead of a spinner.
  
  - **Tap target reuses an unrelated feature's token.** `chat_bubble.dart`'s `buildBookmarkButton` constrains the tap target with `DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin`. The same diff explicitly introduces a standalone `chatBookmarkIconSize` specifically to avoid aliasing an unrelated token (`entriesSearchBarIconSize`), but then turns around and reuses `insertionModalTapTargetMin` (an Insertion Modal concept) for the chat bubble's tap target instead of defining its own `chatBookmarkTapTargetMin` — inconsistent with the stated token-naming philosophy in the same commit.

  - **Duplicated "unused/throwing" fake across four test files.** `_UnusedSaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (or an equivalent throwing fake) is hand-rolled independently in `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`, `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart`, and `test/main_test.dart` (plus a differently-shaped recording fake in `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart`), instead of being factored into a shared helper under `test/support/`, where `fake_connectivity_watcher.dart` already lives.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

input.new_string:
- Given a save fails, when the error state shows, then the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable and the button resets to a retryable `error` state rather than freezing, with state carried by icon + color together.

### Review Findings

- [ ] [Review][Decision] Bookmark save outcome silently dropped on session switch — `bookmarkMessage()` awaits `isolatedSideEffect` then re-reads `state` and rebuilds `messages` by id; `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` (`chat_cubit.dart:206-300`) replace `ChatReady.messages` wholesale and only cancel the send/retry stream (`_cancelInFlightSend`) — never a bookmark save in flight. If the user switches sessions (or starts a new one) while a save is pending, the eventual `saved`/`error` result finds no matching message in the new `ChatReady.messages` and is silently discarded: no confirmation, no error, no retryable state surfaced. Backend idempotency prevents data corruption/duplicate Entries, but the user gets no feedback either way. Needs a product decision: block session switch while a bookmark save is in flight, track the save independent of the active session, or accept the silent loss as-is. [`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:592-624`]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test for `bookmarkMessage()`'s pre-save `isClosed`/non-`ChatReady` guards or cross-message concurrency — only the `isClosed` guard *after* the `isolatedSideEffect` await is tested; the guard before the first `saving` emit, the `current is! ChatReady` early-return, and two independent messages bookmarked concurrently without cross-talk are all unexercised. [`test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart:1344`]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `bookmarkMessage()` tests index `messages[0]`/`messages[1]` directly, reintroducing fragility a nearby helper explicitly avoids — `sendAndCompleteWithServerId`'s own comment says it filters by role "so this helper keeps working if message ordering ever changes... instead of silently asserting on the wrong bubble," but the surrounding assertions in the same group use raw indices instead. [`test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart:1101-1140`]

content.text:
## Code review complete — Story 6.4 (Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry)

**1** `decision-needed`, **4** `patch`, **0** `defer`, **8** dismissed as noise.

Findings written to the Review Findings section in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-4-bookmark-a-chat-message-into-an-entry.md`.

Worth noting on the 8 dismissed: 3 of them (retry-without-checking-`retryable`, `BookmarkError.failure` never read by the UI, no accessibility announcement on save outcome) were independently re-surfaced by the review layers but are already logged with reasoning in this same diff's own `deferred-work.md` addition — I didn't duplicate them. The other 5 were false positives or cosmetic once checked against the actual code: the "unrelated" `insertionModalTapTargetMin` reuse for the tap target is in fact the established cross-feature 44pt-floor token (also used by `entries_search_bar.dart`/`sync_badge.dart`); the two new design tokens follow the file's existing documented precedent for values the prototype doesn't cover; the Reduce-Motion label's 64pt width cap is exactly what the frozen Boundaries asked for (truncate rather than squeeze the bubble); and the bundled `dart format` reformatting / duplicated test fixture were non-functional nits too minor to act on.

## Decision needed

**Bookmark save outcome silently dropped on session switch.** `bookmarkMessage()` awaits the save, then re-reads `state` and rebuilds the message list by id. `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` replace `ChatReady.messages` wholesale and only cancel the send/retry stream — never a bookmark save in flight. If the user switches sessions (or starts a new one) while a save is pending, the result finds no matching message in the new state and is silently discarded: no confirmation, no error, nothing retryable surfaced. Backend idempotency means no duplicate Entry/data corruption — just a confusing "did it save or not?" gap, and it's untested.

This wasn't covered by the spec's Boundaries/I-O matrix, so I can't patch it unambiguously. Options:

1. **Block session switch while a bookmark save is in flight** — simplest, but adds a new UX constraint not currently specced.
2. **Track the save independent of the active session** (e.g. a side map keyed by message id) so the result still applies even after switching back, surfacing it next time that session is viewed.
3. **Defer as-is** — log it in `deferred-work.md` like the sibling `retryable`-gating finding, accepting the current silent-loss behavior for now since it's a narrow timing window and no data is corrupted.

**Reply with just the number (1, 2, or 3).**

Backend idempotency prevents data corruption/duplicate Entries, but the user gets no feedback either way. [`test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart:1101-1140`]

content.content:
99	### Review Findings
100	
101	- [x] [Review][Decision] Bookmark save outcome silently dropped on session switch — `bookmarkMessage()` awaits `isolatedSideEffect` then re-reads `state` and rebuilds `messages` by id; `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` (`chat_cubit.dart:206-300`) replace `ChatReady.messages` wholesale and only cancel the send/retry stream (`_cancelInFlightSend`) — never a bookmark save in flight. If the user switches sessions (or starts a new one) while a save is pending, the eventual `saved`/`error` result finds no matching message in the new `ChatReady.messages` and is silently discarded: no confirmation, no error, no retryable state surfaced. **Resolved:** tracked the save's outcome in a new `_bookmarkStateByServerId` map on `ChatCubit`, keyed by the message's `serverId` (stable across a reload, unlike the in-session local `id`) — same in-memory-only, survives-session-switches lifetime as the existing `_scrollOffsets` map. `_fromDomain` applies any recorded override when a session's history (re)loads, so re-entering a session that carries the bookmarked message picks the outcome back up instead of losing it; the live emit at the end of `bookmarkMessage()` now also matches by `serverId` rather than the possibly-stale local `id`. Chose this over blocking session switches (a new UX constraint the spec never asked for) since it fixes the gap without adding one. New regression test: `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` ("review fix (round 2): a save that resolves after the user has switched sessions..."). [`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:592-624`]
102	- [ ] [Review][Patch] No test for `bookmarkMessage()`'s pre-save `isClosed`/non-`ChatReady` guards or cross-message concurrency — only the `isClosed` guard *after* the `isolatedSideEffect` await is tested; the guard before the first `saving` emit, the `current is! ChatReady` early-return, and two independent messages bookmarked concurrently without cross-talk are all unexercised. [`test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart:1344`]
103	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `bookmarkMessage()` tests index `messages[0]`/`messages[1]` directly, reintroducing fragility a nearby helper explicitly avoids — `sendAndCompleteWithServerId`'s own comment says it filters by role "so this helper keeps working if message ordering ever changes... instead of silently asserting on the wrong bubble," but the surrounding assertions in the same group use raw indices instead. [`test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart:1101-1140`]
104	- [ ] [Review][Patch] New `chat_screen_test.dart` wiring test uses unscoped global icon finders — `find.byIcon(Icons.bookmark_border)`/`find.byIcon(Icons.check)` search the entire pumped `ChatScreen` tree rather than being scoped to the tapped bubble/button, so the test would start matching an unrelated icon elsewhere on screen if one is ever added. [`test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart:728,736`]
105	- [ ] [Review][Patch] Throwing `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` fake duplicated across 5 test files instead of factored into `test/support/` — a near-identical "never expected to be called" fake is hand-rolled independently in `main_test.dart`, `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, `chat_cubit_test.dart`, and `chat_screen_test.dart`, instead of a shared helper (where `fake_connectivity_watcher.dart` already lives).

A bookmark save that resolves after the user switches sessions is no longer silently dropped.
- **`chat_cubit_test.dart`** — new regression test for the session-switch fix, plus three new tests closing the guard/concurrency coverage gaps (pre-save `isClosed`, non-`ChatReady` no-op, two messages bookmarked concurrently with no cross-talk — which caught that the test helper's role-only filter always returns the *first* user message, fixed in the test itself).
